node: Housing repair/remodel contractor supply, specialty distributors, restoration products, equipment rental, and dealer networks
summary: Expanded the universe around the hypothesis that repair/remodel capacity is constrained by contractor-facing distribution density, specialty rental availability, installed-product execution, and last-mile building-products logistics rather than by consumer demand alone. The pass keeps one reference distributor, QXO, as a scale/context anchor, and prioritizes three smaller or less obvious public names: BlueLinx, Installed Building Products, and Herc Rentals. Key chokepoint signals to verify in later layers are branch density, contractor/customer retention, repair/remodel revenue mix, fleet utilization, insurance-restoration exposure, product availability, and whether pricing/margins hold when new-home construction remains soft.
